digest.en: COP31 delegates in Sharm El‑Sheikh pressed for renewed climate action while wars rage across the Middle East and Africa. Meanwhile in London, an Argentinian lawyer mocked the United Kingdom’s claim to sovereignty over the Falklands oil venture.
digest.hi: A 6.2‑meter quake rattled the outskirts of Jeddah’s King Abdulaziz International Airport, shattering windows and forcing emergency evacuations. Despite the tremor, no casualties were reported, but the incident raised questions about seismic preparedness in Saudi Arabia’s growing aviation hub.

articles.title: COP31 leaders urge focus on climate action despite global conflicts
articles.summary: Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are at COP31 seeking agreement on a Turkish proposal. The plan aims to increase electricity's share in global energy use. It also seeks to revive stalled efforts to reduce fossil fuel dependence. Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are seeking agreement at COP31 on a proposal from Turkey to increase the share of electricity in global ‌energy use and revive stalled efforts to move away from fossil fuels.

articles.title: Argentinian lawyer mocks UK’s sovereignty claim in Falklands oil case
articles.summary: Argentina's lawyer Marcelo Kohen mocked Britain's sovereignty claims in a Hamburg tribunal hearing. He argued the UK should not act as a colonial power. Kohen rejected the historic doctrine of British maritime dominance over Falklands waters. Lawyer says Britain wrong to believe in historic doctrine that crown has sovereignty over parts of oceansBritain should not be permitted to act as a 17th-century colonial power treating the waters around the Falkland Islands as a Dominium maris Britannici, Argentina has told an international tribunal. Marcelo Kohen, representing Argentina at a hearing in Hamburg, mocked Britain for apparently belie.

articles.title: Netanyahu dismisses claims that Israel blocking supplies to Gaza
articles.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu dismissed claims that Israel is blocking supplies to Gaza. He blamed Hamas for refusing to disarm under the Trump-announced deal. Netanyahu stated the group seizes humanitarian aid for military use. Benjamin Netanyahu said the Palestinian militant group Hamas is to blame because it continues to refuse to disarm, a condition of the deal announced by Donald Trump, and seizes humanitarian aid in order to use it for military purposes.

articles.title: Killing of journalist underscores deteriorating conditions in Ecuador
articles.summary: Ecuadorian journalist Tomás Beltrán was shot dead while parking his car in Calceta. The killing highlights deteriorating security conditions in the country. Gang warfare over drug routes has made the Pacific coastline a key flashpoint. Tomás Beltrán was shot dead amid gang warfare that has turned Latin American country into one of its most violentTomás Beltrán was manoeuvring his car into his garage on Sunday night when the Ecuadorian journalist was shot dead. Beltrán ran a Facebook page with news about Calceta, a small city in the province of Manabí, whose Pacific coastline has made it a key flashpoint in the gang warfare over d.

articles.title: How Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affair could cause collateral damage in Washington
articles.summary: Federal investigators probe Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over an alleged affair and claims a former executive spied for China. The inquiry examines export controls and national security breaches tied to Nvidia chips. These legal and political issues create significant collateral damage in Washington. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang confronts a widening political and legal storm in Washington over an alleged extramarital affair and claims a former Megaspeed executive spied for China, as federal investigators probe export controls and possible national-security breaches tied to Nvidia’s chips in the high-stakes U. S.-China AI race.

articles.title: U.S. and China should stay clear-eyed on AI cooperation and competition, says Scott Bessent
articles.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent travels to China next week for President Trump’s third meeting with Xi Jinping. He aims to build a constructive relationship based on balance and reciprocity. The visit focuses on maintaining clear-eyed approaches to AI cooperation and competition between the two nations. Bessent, who will travel to China next week for U. S. President Donald Trump’s third meeting this year with Chinese President Xi Jinping, said that he wanted to “build a constructive relationship on the basis of balance and reciprocity”.

articles.title: Wartime memory shows China-Russia ties far from ‘limitless’
articles.summary: China and Russia have aligned their official memories of the Second World War for over a decade. They stage joint commemorations and coordinate remembrance dates. This memory alliance reveals their ties are far from limitless despite shared narratives. For more than a decade, China and Russia have sought to align their official memories of the Second World War. They have staged prominent joint commemorations and military parades, while also coordinating remembrance dates and harmonizing their official discourses about the war.

articles.title: Falkland Islanders face ‘devastating consequences’ if Argentina blocks oil project, says UK
articles.summary: Argentina told the Hamburg tribunal that Britain’s approval of the Sea Lion oil project deepened the Falklands sovereignty dispute. The legal clash marks a historic confrontation over drilling rights in the North Falkland basin. The dispute traces back to the war four decades ago. Sea Lion project in the North Falkland basin threatens to deepen sovereignty disputeArgentina has told an international tribunal that Britain’s approval of oil drilling off the Falkland Islands has dramatically deepened a sovereignty dispute that led to war four decades ago. At the start of an historic legal clash at the Hamburg-based International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (Itlos), an Argent.

articles.title: Moscow Police Detain Hundreds Of Youths, Pressure Those Of Military Age Into Service
articles.summary: Moscow police detained hundreds of youths, including children, during a raid on an alternative gathering. Detainees reported beatings and denial of basic needs. Adults received draft notices or faced pressure to sign army contracts. Police labeled the action a preventive operation. Hundreds, including children, were detained in a raid on an alternative youth gathering in central Moscow. Detainees reported beatings and being denied water and toilets.

articles.title: Ukraine, Russia Negotiators Conclude First Day Of US-Led Peace Talks As Europe Seeks Role
articles.summary: Ukrainian and Russian negotiators concluded the first day of US-brokered peace talks. The two-day session aims to address Moscow’s ongoing war on Ukraine. It remains unclear if any tangible progress was made during the initial session. Ukrainian and Russian negotiators wrapped up the first of two days of US-brokered talks aimed at untangling Moscow's nearly 5-year-old all-out war on Ukraine, though it was unclear what progress there had been, if any.

articles.title: Social Insurance Could Help China Rebalance, If Beijing Enforces It
articles.summary: China introduced new penalty standards for unpaid social insurance contributions. Enforcing these rules would protect retiring workers. It would also boost domestic consumption. This shift could reduce the country's heavy reliance on exports for economic growth. China’s new penalty standards for unpaid social insurance contributions are a positive step. Enforcing the law would not only protect workers in retirement but also help boost domestic consumption and reduce China’s dependence on exports.

articles.title: How much will Jensen Huang’s scandal ultimately cost?
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang. She has been accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent. The scandal raises concerns about the security of artificial intelligence chip supply chains. Jensen Huang, the chief executive and co-founder of chipmaking company Nvidia, recently admitted to an extramarital affair. However, it’s not just a tabloid story: the woman involved, Alice Huang, has been accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent.

articles.title: Nearly 64,000 flee Nigeria for Niger where a humanitarian crisis is deepening
articles.summary: UNHCR reported 64,000 people fled northern Nigeria for Niger this year. Several hundred also left for Benin. Violence in the region is deepening a humanitarian crisis. Host countries are struggling to cope with the sudden influx of displaced residents. Violence in northern Nigeria is fueling a growing humanitarian crisis across the whole region: 64,000 have fled to neighbouring Niger and several hundred have left for Benin since the start of the year, as host countries struggle to cope, the UN’s refugee agency (UNHCR) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: South Sudan’s first elections loom amid rising violence
articles.summary: South Sudan faces its first national elections in six weeks as violence escalates. The Security Council meets in New York to demand credible polls. Civilians continue to suffer from fighting, hunger, and displacement. With South Sudan just six weeks away from its first national elections since independence, the Security Council meets in New York Tuesday amid deepening political uncertainty and worsening violence.

articles.title: First ‘suicide’ drone attacks, now long-range strikes are the norm
articles.summary: UNICEF warns that drones and drought are closing in on Sudan. Attackers now use long-range drones traveling up to 1,500 kilometers. These strikes target critical infrastructure across the country. Drones and drought are “closing in” on Sudan, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF, said on Tuesday, describing unprecedented attacks on the country’s infrastructure including by drones travelling up to 1,500 kilometres before hitting their target.

articles.title: IOM urges wider surveillance beyond formal routes in DR Congo
articles.summary: The International Organization for Migration urged broader surveillance beyond formal routes in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Seventy-one confirmed Ebola cases were detected along transit routes since the outbreak began six months ago. The agency highlighted the need to monitor movement outside standard health checkpoints. Seventy-one confirmed Ebola cases have been detected along transit routes in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) since the outbreak began almost six months ago, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: Fact-checking site’s entire newsroom jailed as assault on press freedom widens
articles.summary: Six journalists from the Egyptian fact-checking site Matsadash remain in detention. The UN human rights office confirmed their continued imprisonment. This incident highlights a widening assault on press freedom. The government faces criticism for targeting independent media operations. Six journalists who make up the entire newsroom of the Egyptian fact-checking website Matsadash remain in detention, the UN human rights office (OHCHR) said on Tuesday, warning of proliferating assaults on press freedom by the Government.

articles.title: Climate crisis could push 141 million more women into extreme poverty
articles.summary: Over one billion women and girls live in climate hotspots. High hazard exposure combines with insecure jobs and gender inequality. The crisis could push 141 million more into extreme poverty. More than one in three women and girls worldwide – roughly 1.5 billion – live in so-called “climate hotspots”, where high exposure to hazards such as cyclones and droughts combine with insecure jobs and deep gender inequality.

articles.title: Europe's Fruitless Search For A Ukraine Peace Envoy; EU Safeguards For Montenegro
articles.summary: The EU cannot agree on a single envoy for Russia-Ukraine peace talks. Meanwhile, Montenegro faces potential safeguards upon joining the bloc. RFE/RL Europe Editor Rikard Jozwiak analyzes both issues in this week's briefing. In this week's briefing, RFE/RL Europe Editor Rikard Jozwiak is drilling down on two issues: why the EU cannot agree on an envoy for Russia-Ukraine peace talks and what safeguards Montenegro could face when it joins the bloc.

articles.title: Don’t let Taiwan’s silicon shield become a US silicon trap
articles.summary: TSMC is investing heavily in US semiconductor fabrication. This brings encouraging news for the struggling US economy. However, reliance on a single foreign supplier creates strategic risks for American supply chains. As the midterms loudly demonstrated, there is considerable gloom over the US economy. Cause for economic optimism is in short supply, though there is some encouraging news regarding US-based semiconductor fabrication spurred by enormous investments from the huge Taiwan company TSMC.

articles.title: Why Pakistan’s Trump card isn’t paying off
articles.summary: Pakistan’s military-led government failed to secure favorable terms from Donald Trump despite aggressive courting. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif promoted cryptocurrency deals and rare-earth minerals at the White House. The strategy prioritized personal praise over structural policy changes. This transactional approach has not yielded the expected diplomatic or economic concessions for Islamabad. Pakistan’s military-led hybrid government did nearly everything it could to woo Donald Trump, from pursuing cryptocurrency deals with members of the Trump family to showcasing the country’s rare-earth mineral potential at the White House.

articles.title: China fast-tracks mobile ICBM to lock down second-strike edge
articles.summary: China has rapidly deployed a new road-mobile intercontinental ballistic missile to strengthen its second-strike capability. The system addresses technical flaws in earlier models and improves survivability. This move accelerates the modernization of its land-based nuclear deterrent against potential adversaries. China’s rapid operational integration of a new type of intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) underscores an accelerating push to modernize its land-based deterrent, addressing key technical vulnerabilities of earlier systems while fortifying second-strike survivability amid an unprecedented nuclear expansion.

articles.title: A time to rethink American power
articles.summary: Democrats won both houses of Congress in a stunning defeat for President Donald Trump. They captured Senate seats in states they had not won in generations. Voters expressed anger over rising prices, government corruption, and the war with Iran. Last Tuesday’s election was a stunning defeat for President Donald Trump. Democrats won both houses of Congress, including Senate races in states they haven’t won in generations.

articles.title: High Hurdles To Progress At New US-Ukraine-Russia Talks
articles.summary: The United States, Ukraine, and Russia meet in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 for their first talks since February. Analysts expect limited progress on ending the war, citing deep structural disagreements and the lack of a unified negotiating position among the three parties. For the first time since February, the US, Ukraine, and Russia meet on November 10-11 for talks aimed at ending the biggest war in Europe since 1945, but expectations of breakthrough are low.

articles.title: Strikes on Ukraine’s power grid, as peace talks loom
articles.summary: Russian forces struck Ukrainian energy infrastructure, threatening millions with a cold winter and increasing civilian casualties. The UN Security Council convened in New York to discuss the crisis. These strikes occurred just before US-backed peace talks were scheduled to begin in Abu Dhabi. The Security Council convenes at 10am in New York on Ukraine. Russian strikes on energy infrastructure are threatening millions with another cold, dark winter, and civilian deaths are climbing sharply.

articles.summary: इजरायल के प्रधानमंत्री बेंजामिन नेतन्याहू ने कहा कि राष्ट्रीय एकता सरकार बनाना अभी भी संभव है। इससे एक दिन पहले उन्होंने संसद में अरब सांसदों पर आतंकवाद का समर्थन करने का आरोप लगाया था। ‘द टाइम्स ऑफ इजरायल’ की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, इजरायल के प्रधानमंत्री बेंजामिन नेतन्याहू ने बुधवार को कहा कि एक ‘राष्ट्रीय एकता सरकार’ (नेशनल यूनिटी गवर्नमेंट) बनाना अभी भी संभव है।

articles.summary: कनाडा के पब्लिक सेफ्टी मंत्री गैरी आनंदसंगरी ने चीन के संपर्क केंद्रों के आरोपों की जांच की घोषणा की। रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक ये केंद्र चीन की पुलिस और सुरक्षा एजेंसियों का प्रतिनिधित्व करते हैं। यह मामला मानवाधिकार संगठन सेफगार्ड डिफेंडर्स की रिपोर्ट के बाद सामने आया। Canada China liaison points: कनाडा के पब्लिक सेफ्टी मंत्री गैरी आनंदसंगरी ने कहा है कि सरकार उन आरोपों की जांच करेगी, जिनमें दावा किया गया है कि चीन ने कनाडा में कई ‘ liaison पॉइंट्स’ यानी संपर्क केंद्र बना रखे हैं।

articles.title: नेतन्याहू पर अरबों के खिलाफ ‘उकसावे और झूठे आरोपों’ का अभियान चलाने का आरोप, मंसूर अब्बास का बड़ा
articles.summary: मंसूर अब्बास ने नेतन्याहू पर अरब समुदाय के खिलाफ झूठे आरोपों का अभियान चलाने का आरोप लगाया। उन्होंने दावा किया कि प्रधानमंत्री के सहयोगी ने संभावित गठबंधन की जानकारी जुटाने के लिए संपर्क किया था। Israel Politics: राम (Ra’am) पार्टी के नेता मंसूर अब्बास ने बुधवार को इजरायल के प्रधानमंत्री बेंजामिन नेतन्याहू पर आरोप लगाया कि वे अपने पद का इस्तेमाल अरब समुदाय के खिलाफ भड़काने के लिए कर रहे हैं।

articles.title: घरों की छतें उड़ाने आ रहा तूफान सेमपाका, 180 की स्पीड और 980 का प्रेशर मचाएगा प्रलय
articles.summary: प्रशांत में तूफान सेमपाका ने 180 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटा की रफ्तार और 980 हेक्टोपास्कल का दबाव बनाया है। मौसम विज्ञान एजेंसी ने हाई अलर्ट जारी कर दिया है। प्रशांत महासागर में कुदरत का बहुत ही डरावना रूप देखने को मिल रहा है. यहां इस साल का 32वां तूफान 'सेमपाका' (Typhoon Cempaka) आ गया है. इस चक्रवात की हवाओं की रफ्तार 180 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटा है.

articles.title: 'उपन्यास से भी ज्यादा रोमांचक', सोनिया गांधी की किताब पर बोले प्रशांत भूषण
articles.summary: वकील प्रशांत भूषण ने सोनिया गांधी की किताब 'बिलॉन्गिंग' की प्रशंसा की। उन्होंने एक्स पर लिखा कि यह किताब किसी उपन्यास से भी अधिक रोमांचक होगी। सिनियर वकील प्रशांत भूषण ने कांग्रेस की पूर्व अध्यक्ष सोनिया गांधी के किताब बिलॉन्गिंग: ए जर्नी ऑफ लव को लेकर बड़ा बयान दिया है. उन्होंने एक्स पर पोस्ट कर लिखा कि मैंने सोनिया गांधी के निजी संस्मरण को अभी तक नहीं पढ़ा है, लेकिन मैं अंदाज़ा लगा सकता हूं कि यह किताब इतनी दिलचस्प होगी कि इसे पढ़ते हुए आप इसे नीचे नहीं रख पाएंगे.

articles.summary: रामदास अठावले ने सोनिया गांधी की किताब पर प्रतिक्रिया दी। उन्होंने कहा कि विदेशी मूल के मुद्दे पर शरद पवार की भूमिका से सहमत नहीं थे। यह टिप्पणी किताब के लॉन्च के बाद आई। केंद्रीय मंत्री रामदास अठावले ने कांग्रेस नेता सोनिया गांधी की किताब बिलॉंगिंग टू द जर्नी ऑफ लव को लेकर बड़ा बयान दिया है. ये किताब लॉन्च होने के बाद से सुर्खियों में बनी हुई है.

articles.summary: बेलगावी में 24 वर्षीय विजय नारायण की हत्या का मामला सामने आया। आरोप है कि मां मीना ने प्रेमी के साथ मिलकर साजिश रची। कुल छह आरोपियों को गिरफ्तार किया गया है। कर्नाटक के बेलगावी से एक चौंकाने वाला मामला सामने आया है, जहां एक मां पर आरोप है कि उसने अपने प्रेमी के लिए अपने ही जवान बेटे की मौत का फरमान सुना दिया.

articles.title: पहले से और हाईटेक होगी CRPF, कामिकेज ड्रोन सिस्टम लेने का प्लान, क्या है खासियत
articles.summary: सीआरपीएफ कामिकेज ड्रोन सिस्टम खरीदने की योजना बना रहा है। इसमें ऑप्टिकल फाइबर और रेडियो फ्रीक्वेंसी तकनीक शामिल होगी। ड्रोन दिन और रात दोनों में काम करेंगे। केंद्रीय रिजर्व पुलिस बल (CRPF) एक ऐसा कामिकेज ड्रोन सिस्टम लेने की योजना बना रहा है, जो ऑप्टिकल फाइबर केबल (OFC) और रेडियो फ्रीक्वेंसी (RF) पर आधारित फर्स्ट पर्सन व्यू (FPV) तकनीक से लैस होगा.

articles.title: ईरान ने घोषित किया अर्जेंटीना की नेवी और एयरफोर्स को आतंकवादी, 8 महीने बाद लिया बदला
articles.summary: ईरान ने अर्जेंटीना की नौसेना और वायुसेना को आतंकवादी संगठन घोषित किया है। इस कदम के पीछे 2019 के एक कानून का हवाला दिया गया है। शिया देश की ओर से अर्जेंटीना की नौसेना और वायुसेना को आतंकवादी संगठन घोषित कर दिया है और इसके पीछे 2019 के एक कानून का हवाला दिया है. ईरान ने घोषित किया अर्जेंटीना की नेवी और एयरफोर्स को आतंकवादी, 8 महीने बाद लिया बदला।
